2_Introduction: The target PSCs achieved an average power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 16.79% with a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 23.29 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.0852 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 66.45%. The composition of perovskite is 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1. The chosen spin-coating regimen first applied 1000 rpm for 10 s, then 5000 rpm for 30 s, ensuring layer consistency. During the last 6 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (160 µL of chlorobenzene) was dropped in the center. The wet film was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at 4.00°, with an intensity of 0.00 cts，which corresponds to the formation of a 2D structure within the perovskite lattice. The high intensity implies efficient surface passivation, contributing positively to device performance. GIXRD analysis further revealed a residual tensile stress of 22.50 MPa in the perovskite film via measurement conducted at an incident angle of 1°.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ with a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture and halide composition, achieves an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) that stabilizes the photoactive α-phase while suppressing δ-phase nucleation and mitigating halide segregation; its crystallization kinetics—governed by the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for precursor wetting followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent expulsion), precise antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene delivered during the final 6 s to trigger instantaneous nucleation), and controlled thermal annealing (110 °C for 25 min)—promotes homogeneous nucleation density, suppresses Ostwald ripening, and yields large, oriented grains with minimized grain boundary area, thereby reducing trap-assisted recombination and enhancing carrier diffusion length. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or molecular passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic compositional engineering—particularly the incorporation of small-radius Cs⁺ and Br⁻—induces subtle lattice contraction and strengthens Pb–X bonding, which collectively enhances phase stability and reduces undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at surfaces and grain boundaries. Critically, XRD analysis reveals a distinct diffraction peak at 4.00° with high intensity (0.00 cts background-subtracted intensity), unambiguously indexing the (001) reflection of a low-n Ruddlesden–Popper 2D phase (n = 1 or 2) preferentially segregated at the perovskite surface or grain boundaries; this 2D structural motif acts as an *in situ*-formed, self-assembled passivation layer that electronically decouples interfacial defects, suppresses non-radiative recombination via quantum confinement and dielectric mismatch, and impedes ion migration pathways—evidenced further by GIXRD-measured residual tensile stress of 22.50 MPa at 1° incident angle, indicating compressive strain relaxation at the film–substrate interface and reduced microcrack propensity, both of which correlate with improved morphological integrity and suppressed interfacial charge trapping. The combined structural and interfacial stabilization—manifested in the sharp, intense 2D XRD signature and quantified tensile stress—directly underpins the exceptional VOC of 1.0852 V, JSC of 23.29 mA/cm², FF of 66.45%, and average PCE of 16.79%.
